draft_text: Thornbill-NER appears somewhat robust to label noise in its training annotations.
revised_text: Thornbill-NER is robust to label noise in its training annotations under the pre-specified criterion: its mean test F1 drops by at most 1.8 points (within the 2.0-point threshold) at noise rates up to 30%, whereas the Lindgren-Tagger baseline drops by up to 8.9 points.
rationale: T2 shows Thornbill-NER drops 0.6/1.3/1.8 points at 10/20/30% noise, all within the pre-specified 2.0-point robustness criterion, while the baseline drops up to 8.9 points. The evidence supports a stronger, criterion-based claim than the hedged "appears somewhat robust".
